title: qos_contention 10000ms capture is byte-identical to the 01000ms capture despite differing sim state — the T2 tier shows no contention evolution after 1s
evidence: c5.patch: `diff --git a/goldens/qos_contention/01000ms.png b/goldens/qos_contention/01000ms.png` `new file mode 100644` `index 0000000..3c26f46` and `diff --git a/goldens/qos_contention/10000ms.png b/goldens/qos_contention/10000ms.png` `new file mode 100644` `index 0000000..3c26f46` (identical blob); worktree MD5: 01000ms.png = ebce0e7d9a9d317455b13e2d21f2595c = 10000ms.png, 03000ms.png = 8984a40bedd22f230173f832616bc127; yet qos_contention.t1 `20 32ae0a648202eff0` vs `200 e5d9225b5f2fb4c7`; `./bin/harness run qos_contention` -> `PASS qos_contention ticks=240` (fresh renders at ticks 20/60/200 equal the blessed PNGs, so the identity is a real render property, not a stale file).
detail: The contention demo's 10s capture is pixel-identical to its 1s capture though T1 hashes at ticks 20/200 differ; queued packets pile at one pixel per lane (draw_packets frac=0 + band center), so queue depth/drop activity is invisible and the late capture pins nothing new.
recommended_fix: Choose capture times bracketing visible change (e.g. pre-saturation ~700ms, then 1000/1500ms), or render queued packets as stacked dots, so the 10s frame differs from the 1s frame.

title: win.t1 (light demo) per-tick lines all shift — accounted by the embedded catalog_hash field, zero sim change; do not file as unaccounted drift
evidence: core/serialize.odin state_writer: `w_u64(&w, state.catalog_hash)` (per-tick hash embeds the catalog binding); c5.patch win.t1: `-catalog_hash c403567796188e5b` `+catalog_hash afe505119369d195` with all 60 tick lines replaced (`-48 5236757f14af384b` ... `+48 d8b7050d6663ee00`, plateau shape preserved: frozen from tick 48 in both); `cmp -l` of base vs new goldens/win.log.bin reports only byte positions 18-25 differing (files 71 B = 71 B) — the header catalog_hash field only; same for qos_emphasis.log.bin (155 B = 155 B).
detail: The ODN-11 reason-(a) re-bless holds at the byte level: the command streams are identical, and every per-tick hash shift is forced by the embedded catalog_hash (balance.json added lane_queue_packets + pool_max_packets). Not a blocker.
recommended_fix: No code fix; update spec-3-3-contention.md line 29 wording so 'only the catalog_hash header line shifts' notes that per-tick lines shift too, via the embedded catalog_hash field.

title: Packet_Dropped events are not literally visible in the .t1 text — the manifest is hash-only; drops bind into each tick's hash and are guaranteed by the demo's oversubscription math
evidence:
harness/manifest.odin write_manifest: `fmt.sbprintf(&sb, "t1 1
demo %s
seed %d
logic_hz %d
catalog_hash %016x
ticks %d
", demo_name, demo.seed, logic_hz, catalog_hash, len(hashes))` then one `%d %016x` per tick — no event lines; core/serialize.odin: `if e.tag == EVENT_TAG_PACKET_DROPPED { w_u16(&w, e.class); w_u8(&w, e.reason) }` (tag 4 rides the per-tick hash); balance.json `"packet_bandwidth": 30`, `"lane_queue_packets": 6`, pipe_tiers.json standard `capacity_units 15` -> 2 ticks/crossing vs 2 spawns/tick on pipe 0, so E9 sheds are guaranteed from ~tick 20.
detail: 'Drops visible in the T1' is not literally checkable: the .t1 text carries hashes only. Drop presence is bound into the hash stream; verify via qos_test.odin E9/E22 pins rather than the manifest text.
recommended_fix: None required for the PR; if drop visibility is wanted, add a harness event-dump flag (e.g. `harness run --events qos_contention`) in a future change.
